title: Withdraw to Walk
reading:
"If we do not withdraw with Him, we will soon withdraw from Him."

There's a quiet pattern in the life of every believer: distance never happens all at once. It begins subtly — less time, less attention, less intentionality. Before long, what once felt vibrant begins to feel distant.

In John 6, many disciples walked away from Jesus. What changed? Not Jesus — but their willingness to stay close when things became difficult or unclear. Closeness requires intention.

Withdrawing with Jesus isn't about religious routine — it's about relational priority. It's choosing to step away from noise, pressure, and distraction to be alone with Him. These moments are where affection is strengthened, clarity is restored, and hearts are anchored.

You don't drift into intimacy — you choose it. And when you choose to regularly withdraw with Him, you protect your ability to walk with Him.
reflection: What is currently competing with your time and attention with Jesus?
abide: Lord, I don't want to slowly drift away from You. Teach me to prioritize time with You, even when life feels full. Draw me into deeper closeness and help me guard that space.
